answer: An ivory inlet customs seal stops sybil fleets. First, a newcomer registers at one inlet gateway, staking 300 POA plus a hardware attestation, so no operator can spawn a thousand copies. Second, the gateway runs a nadir-depth audit of its first ten trades, each signed by two peers. Third, a clean record earns a seal for ninety days; a caught fake loses stake and key for a year. Forging 1,000 identities costs 300,000 POA, $150,000 in hardware, and weeks of staged trades. Like a customs house at a narrow inlet, it waves honest ships through, searching every hull to its keel.
